title: InfraPulse failure handoff and rollback ops sync
summary: Follow-up bridge to hand off RCA items from last week's outage, align on rollback/failed-deploy playbook changes, confirm observability gaps (trace retention, KV cache metrics), and agree next steps for pilot hardening and SLA credits discussion.
action_items: Jordan Ellis - Send annotated rollback runbook + short video demo - due 2027-06-18
Priya Kapoor - Provide KV cache crash log excerpts and suspected patch diff - due 2027-06-17
Marcus Li - Propose trace retention config and cost delta estimate - due 2027-06-20
Nina Park (InfraPulse) - Share internal incident timeline and list of downstream teams affected - due 2027-06-16
Sana Qureshi (InfraPulse) - Grant temp access to staging logs bucket for Redwood SEs - due 2027-06-15
next_steps: Redwood to provide a patched KV cache PR candidate and test harness
Schedule a runbook walkthrough + dry-run on staging (45 min) next Tue
Agree on SLA remediation language and credit proposal by EOW
Set up dedicated pilot with 2x autoscale headroom for three days of traffic replay
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-14 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood SRE), Aisha Gomez (Redwood CSM); Nina Park (InfraPulse VP Eng), Leo Martinez (Platform Lead), Sana Qureshi (SRE), Tom B. (Procurement)

Summary: quick follow-up to the incident on 2027-06-08 where a KV cache corruption triggered cascading timeouts and a partial failover to lower-capacity hosts. Goal is to align on runbook, tests and pilot timeline.

[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, uh I think we have a full table, we wanted to make this fairly tactical - handoff from the incident team into the remediation workstreams. I can quick recap and then hand to Priya for the SE technical bits.
[00:28] Nina Park: Thanks. quick note, we had exec pressure after the outage, so timeline is kinda tight, we need clear dates.
[00:36] Priya Kapoor: Understood. Yesterday's RCA showed two main drivers: an edge-case in prefix-KV cache eviction logic combined with a malformed async retry that retriggered stale entries, and then on our side the autoscaler didn't prioritize cultivating fresh warm VMs so cold starts amplified latency.
[01:05] Leo Martinez: Sorry can you repeat the prefix-KV cache bit, I'm not sure I heard the eviction bit right.
[01:12] Priya Kapoor: Yeah so the cache eviction policy used an LRU window that assumed monotonically increasing sequence ids, but under some request reordering we saw sequence ids arrive out of order, which left orphaned pointers in the KV index. That leads to a read path returning empty but still decrementing the reference counter, eventually hitting a race where the cache layer tried to compact indexes and borked the in-memory map. It's kinda like missing a tombstone.
[01:43] Sana Qureshi: That matches our stack traces, we saw NullPointer-ish crashes coming from cache.compact but some of the names in the stack aren't matching, probably because of symbol stripping in our build.
[01:54] Marcus Li: We also noticed GC pauses aligned with the compaction window, which made the timing windows worse. If compaction holds the lock during a minor GC it can cascade.
[02:10] Jordan Ellis: Right, so short term we need a rollback safety net and then a patch path: rollback + hardened compaction + test harness.

[02:22] Priya Kapoor: For rollback, we propose a two-stage fallback: first route requests to a hot-standby model pool (lower cap but stable) while spinning up a repaired pool. Second, if latency still exceeds threshold, divert long-running paths to the small-model fallback with reduced context to keep SLAs partially met.
[02:45] Leo Martinez: Curious about the small-model fallback — that sounds like it might change output format for downstream; we can't have consumers re-ingest differently shaped responses.
[02:55] Priya Kapoor: Good point, Leo — we can shim a translator so the surface contract is preserved, e.g. trim nonessential tokens but keep schema fields. There is some nuance — quality will vary but it's deterministic.
[03:15] Nina Park: How long would a typical rollback take? We ran into a rollback before that took 20 mins and then hit the same bug on the older version.
[03:25] Marcus Li: Our rollback checklist is usually 10-25 minutes validated, but the key is the preflight: do we have a clean cached snapshot and verified warm hosts. If hosts are cold it stretches. For this infra we recommend a 2-phase dry run in staging first, then a canary.
[03:46] Jordan Ellis: I'm going to send the annotated rollback runbook after this call. It includes canary thresholds and post-rollback verification steps.

[04:00] [Speaker: Tom B.] Tom B.: quick procurement note: any changes to config, does that require a contract amendment? We have a SLO addendum in play.
[04:08] Aisha Gomez: Normally not for ops tweaks, but SLA credits or reserved capacity will go through your account team; Jordan can follow up on the credit proposal.
[04:19] Jordan Ellis: Yep, we'll include that in the EOW remediation proposal.

[04:28] Priya Kapoor: On the patch — we have a candidate change that makes the compaction idempotent and adds guardrails around the eviction window; it also emits a new metric kv.cache.tombstone_rate and a debug trace when a compaction detects out-of-order sequence ids. We want to run it behind a feature flag for a couple days in staging.
[04:52] Sana Qureshi: Can we see those metric names? We need to map them into our Grafana.
[04:57] Priya Kapoor: Yes, I'll paste the metric names and sample PromQL in the follow-up.

[05:06] Leo Martinez: Observability gap — we don't retain traces long enough to catch the pre-failure spikes. We only keep 24 hours, but the incident window was 30+ hours from first anomaly to failure.
[05:20] Marcus Li: We can increase retention on the service trace to 72 hours for the pilot; cost delta is small for a single service but we'll share a cost estimate.
[05:33] Nina Park: We need an explicit cost vs risk number — ops will sign for it if it's within budget.
[05:40] Marcus Li: I'll push that in the action items.

[05:49] Priya Kapoor: A second mitigation is a shadow write to persistent backing store for critical keys during compaction windows; it reduces cache performance but adds safety. We can run shadow writes for a narrow subset of keys.
[06:05] Leo Martinez: That might be acceptable. We'll need to coordinate retention and eviction windows in our own LRU policy too.

[06:18] Jordan Ellis: On test harness, Redwood will provide a small-scale replay that reproduces the sequence id reordering in staging. It uses a traffic mutator to inject reorder and delay.
[06:31] Sana Qureshi: Can that run in our existing staging without a lot of infra changes?
[06:36] Priya Kapoor: Yes, it's a sidecar script and a few feature flags. We can also run it in a Redwood sandbox environment if you prefer isolation.

[06:47] [00:07:00] Nina Park: Wanted to raise downstream alerts — our payments team saw a retry storm which retriggered rate limits and we hit a third-party outage window. We need to include downstream mitigation in the runbook.
[07:10] Jordan Ellis: Agreed, runbook will include downstream notification templates and throttling knobs.

[07:20] Leo Martinez: Security/compliance question — does any of the proposed telemetry sharing require PII transfer? Our compliance team is sensitive.
[07:29] Marcus Li: No PII, it's all internal request ids and traces. We can redact any fields if you want.
[07:35] Nina Park: We'll ask compliance to check the sample logs. Sana will share the list.

[07:45] Priya Kapoor: On dedicated vs hosted fallbacks: we recommend a brief switch to a dedicated pool for the pilot to avoid noisy neighbor issues while we test the patch. It reduces routing complexity and gives better SLA isolation.
[08:02] Leo Martinez: Does that require Reserved Capacity contract?
[08:07] Jordan Ellis: For short pilots we can broker temporary dedicated headroom without a full reserved contract; it's handled as a pilot addendum. Tom, we'll loop procurement when we submit the credit/provisioning ask.

[08:20] [00:09:00] Tom B.: Sounds reasonable as long as pricing and stop-gap are clear.

[09:00] Priya Kapoor: Quick note about postmortem language — we'll include a lineage of requests and the exact commit hash that introduced the compaction change, plus the diff. We may redact internal dev comments.
[09:15] Nina Park: Good. Also, we want the postmortem to be customer-facing and a separate internal RCA; two versions.

[09:25] Marcus Li: On the runbook dry-run: propose doing a 'dry-rollback' in staging where we simulate the timing and verify the canary verification steps don't trigger false positives. That takes about 45 minutes and needs the staging trace retention increased to 48h during the test.
[09:45] Priya Kapoor: We'll supply the dry-run checklist. It's mostly a sequence: mark canary route, inject reordering, verify kv.cache.tombstone_rate is zeroing after fix, then execute rollback if verification fails, then post-run validation.

[10:10] Leo Martinez: How do we validate that the compaction fix actually prevents the orphan pointers? Are there synthetic asserts?
[10:17] Priya Kapoor: Yes we added a debug assert that fails in staging on detection of an orphan pointer; it will raise a non-fatal metric so you can watch without crashing prod.

[10:30] [00:11:30] Jordan Ellis: Ok to recap: Redwood provides patch candidate behind flag, test harness, rollback runbook, and cost estimate for trace retention. InfraPulse to share internal timeline, staging access and confirm pilot window.
[11:00] Sana Qureshi: On access — we will create a temporary role with read-only access to the staging logs and grant it to two Redwood SEs.
[11:08] Jordan Ellis: Thanks. We'll only use it for the test harness and then the role will be removed.

[11:18] Nina Park: Execs asked for a projected mitigation timeline. Can you commit to dates?
[11:24] Jordan Ellis: Tentative: runbook + rollback video by Friday (2027-06-18), KV patch PR and test harness by 2027-06-21, staging dry-run during week of 2027-06-22, pilot hardening the following week. We can tighten as we exchange artifacts.
[11:43] Nina Park: That is helpful.

[11:50] Marcus Li: I'll quantify the retention cost and the estimated perf hit for shadow writes, along with a short A/B run plan.
[12:02] Priya Kapoor: I'll also include sample PromQL and Grafana snippets for kv.cache.tombstone_rate and compaction latency percentiles.

[12:12] Jordan Ellis: Any other risks or blockers?
[12:15] Leo Martinez: Compatibility with downstream parsers — make sure the fallback translator preserves the JSON schema strictly.
[12:22] Priya Kapoor: We'll add a schema conformance test to the harness.

[12:30] [00:12:45] Tom B.: Procurement will review pilot addendum. I'll be the contact for commercial terms.
[12:36] Jordan Ellis: Great. We'll send a proposed addendum along with the credit proposal.

[12:45] [00:13:00] Closing remarks: Jordan - will follow up with artifacts; Nina - will circulate internal incident timeline; Sana - will create staging access; Marcus - cost numbers; Priya - metrics + harness; Tom - procurement contact.

[13:00] Jordan Ellis: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the dry-run and I'll send calendar invites after the follow-ups land.
[13:12] Nina Park: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
